# Implementation Plan: Crews protocol — canonical envelope field addresses (route producers through buildEnvelope + enforce via CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA=1)

<!-- ralph-meta {"overviewTaskId":"crews-protocol-envelope-canonical-fields"} -->

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` (autonomous, member spawn) on 2026-05-30. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan <job_dir>/plan.md --autonomous`.*

## Overview

The crews plugin (`D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/`, v2.2.2) ships a runtime envelope schema framework at `hooks/protocol/envelope.js` (`validateEnvelope`, `buildEnvelope`, `validateOutboxRow`, `kindEnum`) with `CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA=1` enforcement. The brainstorm `crews-summary-rendering-audit` (`c52c0360`) established that this framework is **dead code on the producer side**: only `validateOutboxRow` is consumed (by `mailbox.js:578` inside `appendOutboxBatch`), while `buildEnvelope` and `validateEnvelope` have ZERO production call-sites despite being exported and tested. Every cross-actor write — outbox rows from `stop.js`, `appendSystemMailbox` notifications from `actors.js`/`commands/*`/`threads.js`/`stop.js`, and the lead→member `appendMailbox` path from `send-to-member.js` — constructs envelope-shaped objects ad-hoc. That gap is why v1.7.2's silent `summary` drop escaped: no producer touched the validator that would have caught the wrong field address.

This plan makes the framework load-bearing in three steps: (1) declare canonical addresses per field (extending `validateEnvelope` with explicit per-field rules), (2) route every producer through `buildEnvelope()` so the validator actually runs, and (3) add one round-trip contract test per (producer call-site, consumer code-path) pair plus enable `CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA=1` in the test runner so the contract is enforced on every PR. The v1.7.3 `summary` read-fallback + write-mirror stays in place as the documented transition strategy; v1.8.x removes one half per the canonical-address decision below.

The asymmetries the brainstorm documented as **intentional** (`row.kind` vs `row.from.kind` are semantically distinct fields, not drift; `replyTo` top-level on outbox vs `payload.replyToId` on system-mailbox is a rename + nesting decision) are preserved by the validator with explicit comments — the schema codifies them so future code cannot accidentally collapse them.

## Research Findings

### Codebase Context

Seeded from brainstorm: `D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/brainstorms/crews-summary-rendering-audit/selected-direction.md` (D-001) committed at `c52c0360`. The brainstorm's catalog tables are the source of truth for which (producer, consumer) pairs exist for each field; this plan refers to them by file:line rather than restating.

**Schema framework already shipped (`hooks/protocol/envelope.js`, 78 lines, v1.6+):**

- `kindEnum` — 14-value frozen array covering report kinds (`progress`, `question`, `done`, `blocked`) plus envelope/routing kinds (`message`, `thread-notification`, `thread-fanout`, `member-reply`, `spawn-prompt`, `stop-request`, `proactive-report`, `member-left`, `member-joined`, `system`).
- `validateEnvelope(env, opts)` — currently validates `kind`, `from`, `to`, `payload`, `replyTo`, `id`, `sentAt`. Returns `true` or calls `fail()` which throws in strict mode or appends a `schema-warning:` log line otherwise. **Does NOT currently validate `summary` at all** — that omission is the root of the v1.7.2 silent-drop bug.
- `validateOutboxRow(row, opts)` — validates outbox row shape (kind ∈ {progress, question, done, blocked}, seq, id, writtenAt, from, summary, body, message, replyTo, acks, decisions, hops). **Already wired** at `mailbox.js:578` inside `appendOutboxBatch`, so outbox rows DO get strict validation today.
- `buildEnvelope({kind, from, to, payload, replyTo, sentAt, id})` — factory that fills defaults (`id = crypto.randomUUID()`, `to = null`, `payload = {}`, `replyTo = null`, `sentAt = new Date().toISOString()`) and calls `validateEnvelope(env, { strict: true })`. **Zero callers from `hooks/**/*.js`** — only the test at `tests/protocol-envelope.test.js` uses it.
- Strict mode triggered by `opts.strict === true` OR `process.env.CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA === '1'`.

The remaining producers (`stop.js` outbox writes × 2, `send-to-member.js`, `send-to-thread.js`) each need an individual wrap.

### Technical Constraints

- **No build step.** Crews is pure CommonJS Node 18+. The validator runs at producer-write-time in-process — no TS, no compile-time check.
- **No GitHub Actions workflow exists for crews today** (verified: `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/.github/workflows/` empty; `plugins/crews/.github/` has only `plugin/plugin.json`). "CI" in this plan means: (a) `node tests/run.js` (the 218-test parallel runner already in use) MUST exit zero with `CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA=1` set; (b) the existing `tests/protocol-envelope.test.js` is extended with one round-trip per producer→consumer pair; (c) an optional GitHub Actions workflow is added as a stretch deliverable in story S7. The plan does NOT block on creating the workflow file — the strict-mode test invocation is the primary enforcement.
- **`validateOutboxRow` is already strict-active** at `mailbox.js:578` (`validateOutboxRow(persisted, { cwd, strict: false })` — wait, currently `strict: false` so it warns rather than throws). Strict-mode-in-tests means the warn-vs-throw policy flips: with `CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA=1` the env override makes `strict()` return true regardless of `opts.strict`. **Verify the existing outbox tests don't write malformed rows that currently pass under `strict:false`** — this is risk R1 below.
- **v1.7.3 dual-fix is load-bearing today.** Cannot remove either half (`review-mail.js:111` read-fallback OR `stop.js:840` write-mirror for `payload.summary`) in this plan — that's the explicit follow-up `crews-envelope-summary-canonical-cleanup`. This plan ONLY adds the contract; the cleanup is a separate task.
- **Asymmetries to preserve, not "fix":**
  - `row.kind` (report kind ∈ {progress, question, done, blocked}) vs `row.from.kind` (routing kind ∈ full `kindEnum`) are two semantically distinct fields with overlapping names. The validator must enforce both with separate rules; the catalog/JSDoc must document the distinction.
  - `payload.replyToId` (on system-mailbox `member-reply` notifications) vs top-level `replyTo` (on outbox rows + `send-to-member` mailbox writes) is a deliberate rename: `replyToId` references an **outbox row id** for member-reply lookup, while `replyTo` references the **prior mailbox envelope id** that this message is responding to. The validator codifies both as legal at their respective addresses.

## Approach

### Architecture

The schema is the contract; the producer-wrapping is the enforcement; the round-trip tests are the audit. Each field gets ONE canonical wire address; non-canonical addresses are explicitly rejected in strict mode. Two-address read-fallbacks (`review-mail.js:111`, `review-mail.js:84-85`) stay in place to consume legacy on-disk envelopes during transition but produce a deprecation log line when the non-canonical address is the only present one — that log line becomes the migration signal for the `summary-canonical-cleanup` follow-up.

**Per-field canonical addresses (decisions):**

| Field | Canonical address | Rationale | Asymmetry / exception |
|---|---|---|---|
| `summary` | **top-level** on outbox rows AND system-mailbox envelopes AND `send-to-member`/`send-to-thread` mailbox envelopes | (a) Brainstorm catalog: `mailbox.js:617`, `mailbox.js:713`, `format-progress-tail.js:15`, `send-to-member.js:95`, `stop.js:782` all already write/read top-level; (b) only `stop.js:840` mirrors to `payload.summary` (v1.7.3 fix); (c) one canonical address simplifies the next-minor cleanup. | `payload.summary` on system-mailbox notifications stays as TRANSITIONAL DUPLICATE through v2.3.x (this plan), deprecated in v2.4.x via the `summary-canonical-cleanup` follow-up. Validator warns if `payload.summary` is set without top-level `summary` (silent-drop pattern) and rejects in strict mode. |
| `kind` | **top-level** on every envelope (report kind on outbox rows; routing kind on system-mailbox via `from.kind`) | Already the existing pattern; `kindEnum` already enforced at top-level. | `from.kind` is a SEPARATE field (routing kind) with its OWN validator rule. The validator must NOT collapse `env.kind === env.from.kind` — they can differ legitimately (outbox row with `kind: 'done'` from a member whose `from.kind: 'member-reply'` routing). |
| `replyTo` | **top-level** on outbox rows AND on `send-to-member`/`send-to-thread` mailbox envelopes | Already the existing pattern; `validateOutboxRow` validates it. | `payload.replyToId` on system-mailbox `member-reply` notifications is a DIFFERENT FIELD (references outbox row id, not envelope id) and stays at its current address. Validator has a separate rule for it on `kind: 'member-reply'` system-mailbox envelopes. |
| `progressTail` | **`payload.progressTail`** (nested-only) | Already the existing pattern; all 3 consumers (`review-mail.js:105`, `format-progress-tail.js:2`, `mailbox.js:617` digest builder) read from `payload`. | No top-level mirror permitted; validator rejects top-level `progressTail` in strict mode. |
| `decision` | N/A (not an envelope field; lives on dedicated decision rows) | Brainstorm catalog confirmed. | Out of envelope schema scope. |
| `ack` | N/A (parsed from report tag, transformed to `decision`) | Brainstorm catalog confirmed. | Out of envelope schema scope. |
| `reviewedSeq` | N/A (manifest field, not envelope) | Brainstorm catalog confirmed. | Out of envelope schema scope. |
| `bodyResolution` | N/A (synthesized client-side in `review-mail.js:114` from `resolveBodyFromOutbox`) | Brainstorm catalog confirmed. | Out of envelope schema scope. |
| `from` | **top-level object**, with subfields `role`, `name`, `crew`, `kind`, `triggeredBy` | Already required by `validateEnvelope`. | Validator extends to enforce subfield types (`role ∈ {lead, member, system}`, `name: string`, `crew: string`, `kind ∈ kindEnum or null`). |
| `to` | **top-level**, `string | object | null` | Already required. | No change. |
| `id` | **top-level**, non-empty string (UUID) | Already required. | No change. |
| `sentAt` | **top-level**, ISO-8601 string | Already required. | No change. |
| `payload` | **top-level object** (optional, defaults to `{}`) | Already required when present. | Subfield validation is per-`kind` (rule table below). |

**Per-kind `payload` subfield rules** (extended in `validateEnvelope`):

| `env.kind` | Required `payload.*` | Forbidden `payload.*` | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `member-reply` | `replyToId: string`, `memberName: string`, `outboxSeq: number`, `outboxId: string` | `summary` (because top-level is canonical) | Validator rejects in strict mode if `payload.summary` is present and top-level `summary` is absent (silent-drop guard). |
| `proactive-report` | (none required beyond optional `entries`, `progressTail`) | `summary` mirror without top-level | Same silent-drop guard. |
| `thread-fanout` | `thread: string` | — | — |
| `member-joined` | `memberName: string`, `joinedAt: string` | — | — |
| `member-left` | `memberName: string`, `leftAt: string`, `archived: boolean`, `removedThreads: array` | — | — |
| `stop-request` | `stoppedAt: string`, `leadName: string`, `reasonText: string | null` | — | — |
| `spawn-prompt` | (free-form per-spawn payload) | — | — |
| `message`, `progress`, `question`, `done`, `blocked` | — | top-level `progressTail` (must be nested) | — |
| `system` | — | — | Free-form. |

These rules are **additive** — `validateEnvelope` keeps its current top-level checks and ADDs the per-kind payload rules via a per-kind dispatch table inside the function. This keeps the validator a single file under 200 lines.

### Implementation Strategy

The implementation order matters because S4 (CI enforcement) will fail loudly until S1–S3 land. Run them in this order:

1. **S1 — Extend `validateEnvelope` with canonical-address rules** (no producer changes yet). Add `summary` validation, per-kind `payload` rules, `from` subfield rules, and the explicit-rejection rules above. Unit-test each rule in isolation in a new `tests/protocol-envelope-canonical.test.js`. Strict-mode behaviour: each new rule throws on violation when `opts.strict === true || process.env.CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA === '1'`; otherwise logs a `schema-warning:` line.
2. **S2 — Route the chokepoint through `buildEnvelope`** — modify `mailbox.js:466 appendSystemMailbox` to construct envelopes via `buildEnvelope({kind, from, to, payload, replyTo, sentAt})`. The 7 call-sites that go through this sink (join-crew, member-left, lead-stopped-you, ask-user-question, thread-fanout, member-reply notify, proactive-report fanout) get free coverage. Verify each producer's existing test still passes after the wrap.
3. **S3 — Route the remaining producers individually** — wrap each of `stop.js:782` (`appendOutbox` canonical), `stop.js:839` (`appendOutbox` empty-body retry), `commands/send-to-member.js:93`, `commands/send-to-thread.js` through `buildEnvelope` (outbox writes) or through `buildEnvelope` + `appendMailbox` (mailbox writes). Note `buildEnvelope` is currently shaped for ENVELOPES, not outbox-rows: outbox writes need a sibling `buildOutboxRow({seq, kind, summary, message, replyTo, sessionId, hops?})` factory that calls `validateOutboxRow(row, { strict: true })`. Add that factory in S1.
4. **S4 — Enable `CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA=1` for the test runner.** Modify `tests/run.js` to set `CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA=1` in the env it passes to each worker (unless explicitly overridden by per-test). Run the full 218-test suite locally; fix any pre-existing tests that produce malformed envelopes (these are bugs, not test changes). Document the env var in `README.md` (it's already mentioned at line 204 — extend the description to say "REQUIRED in CI; defaults off in production for backward compat through v2.3.x").
5. **S5 — Round-trip contract test** — add `tests/protocol-envelope-roundtrip.test.js` that for each (producer, consumer) pair in the brainstorm catalog: (a) constructs the producer envelope via the production code path (calling `appendOutbox` / `appendSystemMailbox` / `appendMailbox` against a tempdir), (b) reads back via the consumer code path (calling `formatReviewMailEntry` / `truncateProgressSummary` / `formatOutboxEntries` / `format-progress-tail`), (c) asserts the field value survives the round-trip non-empty. Pairs to cover (from brainstorm catalog):
   - `stop.js:782 appendOutbox` → `review-mail.js:111` (summary, kind, replyTo)
   - `stop.js:831 appendSystemMailbox` → `review-mail.js:111` (summary, including the v1.7.3 fallback path)
   - `stop.js:831 appendSystemMailbox` → `mailbox.js:713 formatOutboxEntries` (summary top-level)
   - `stop.js:831 appendSystemMailbox` → `format-progress-tail.js:15` via `mailbox.js:617` digest builder (summary top-level)
   - `send-to-member.js:93` → `review-mail.js:111` (summary)
   - `stop.js:1006 appendSystemMailbox` (member-reply) → `findActorBySendHistoryId` consumer path (payload.replyToId asymmetry)
   - `stop.js:871` (proactive-report with `payload.progressTail`) → `review-mail.js:105` + `format-progress-tail.js:2` (nested-only)
   - `mailbox.js:appendOutboxBatch` strict-validator pass: a synthesized malformed row with `summary: 123` (number) must throw under `CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA=1`.
6. **S6 — Regression test for v1.7.2 summary-drop** — add a single test in `tests/protocol-envelope-roundtrip.test.js` that constructs an envelope with `payload.summary` ONLY (no top-level `summary`) via direct file write to the mailbox JSONL, runs `review-mail`, asserts the entry surfaces with the summary from `payload.summary` (the v1.7.3 fallback) AND asserts a `schema-warning:` log line was emitted naming the non-canonical address. This is the test that would have FAILED pre-v1.7.3 and locks the contract in place.
7. **S7 — Documentation + (stretch) GitHub Actions workflow** — update `plugins/crews/docs/protocol.md` with the canonical-address catalog (verbatim from the "Per-field canonical addresses" table above). Update `plugins/crews/README.md` line 204 entry on `CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA` to reflect the new required-in-CI status and the per-kind payload rules. Add `plugins/crews/CHANGELOG.md` entry noting the canonical-address decisions per field, the transitional `payload.summary` deprecation timeline, and a forward pointer to `crews-envelope-summary-canonical-cleanup` for the cleanup. Stretch: add `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/.github/workflows/crews-tests.yml` that runs `node plugins/crews/tests/run.js` with `CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA=1` on PRs touching `plugins/crews/**`.

## Scope

### In Scope

- Defining canonical-per-field-address rules for `summary`, `kind`, `from.kind`, `replyTo`, `payload.replyToId`, `progressTail`, `from.*` subfields.
- Extending `hooks/protocol/envelope.js` with the rules and a `buildOutboxRow` factory.
- Routing all 11 enumerated producer call-sites through `buildEnvelope`/`buildOutboxRow` (directly or via the `appendSystemMailbox` chokepoint).
- Enabling `CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA=1` in `tests/run.js`.
- One round-trip contract test per (producer, consumer) pair in the brainstorm catalog.
- One regression test reproducing the v1.7.2 summary-drop bug at the envelope-write level.
- Documentation updates (`docs/protocol.md`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`).
- Stretch: a GitHub Actions workflow that runs the crews test suite on PR.

### Out of Scope

- **Removing the v1.7.3 `summary` dual-fix.** That's `crews-envelope-summary-canonical-cleanup` — explicit follow-up. Both the read-fallback (`review-mail.js:111`) and write-mirror (`stop.js:840`) stay in place this minor; the validator merely emits a deprecation warning when the non-canonical address is the only present one.
- **Renaming `payload.replyToId` to `payload.replyTo` on system-mailbox `member-reply` envelopes.** That's `crews-envelope-replyto-field-name-unification` — breaking change, deferred to v2.0.0 (separate task per brainstorm follow-up #3).
- **Renaming `row.from.kind` to `row.from.routingKind`.** That's `crews-envelope-kind-routing-rename` — breaking change, deferred (follow-up #2).
- **Migrating crews to TypeScript or introducing a build step.** Existing CommonJS validator is sufficient.
- **Changing on-disk envelope storage format.** Validator runs at write-time only; existing on-disk JSONL files are read with the v1.7.3 fallback unchanged.
- **Body-canonical schema work** for `message` vs `body` vs `text` fields — that's the parallel brainstorm `crews-envelope-body-canonical-for-all-kinds`, must complete before its plan reuses this validator extension.
- **`kind`-semantics changes** from the `crews-lead-suppress-kind-tag` brainstorm.
- **Codexu-side changes.** Only `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/` is touched by the impl. The lead's `.ralph-overview/data.json` bookkeeping update happens after merge, not in this plan.

## Risk Areas

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| R1 — Existing producer tests construct malformed envelopes that today pass under `strict: false` and will fail when S4 flips the runner to `CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA=1`. | HIGH | Run the full suite at the END of S1 (before S4) with `CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA=1` set locally. Each failure is either: (a) a real producer-shape bug to fix in S2/S3, or (b) a test that intentionally exercises malformed input and needs `process.env.CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA = '0'` per-test opt-out. Document the per-test opt-out in S4. |
| R2 — `buildEnvelope` currently calls `validateEnvelope(env, { strict: true })` unconditionally — routing every producer through it makes EVERY production write strict, not just CI. | MEDIUM | Make the strictness CI-controlled: `buildEnvelope` reads `process.env.CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA === '1'` to pick strict mode; in production it logs `schema-warning:` and continues (matching today's `validateOutboxRow` behavior at `mailbox.js:578`). The CI run is the gate; production is fail-open. This matches operator preference per AGENTS.md ("the framework is the contract; CI is the enforcement"). |
| R3 — The asymmetry between `row.kind` (report kind) and `row.from.kind` (routing kind) gets accidentally collapsed when extending `validateEnvelope` — e.g., the validator adds a rule `env.kind === env.from.kind`. | MEDIUM | Add a dedicated unit test in `tests/protocol-envelope-canonical.test.js` asserting that an envelope with `kind: 'done'` and `from.kind: 'member-reply'` validates clean. Add a JSDoc comment above the kind-rule block referencing this plan section. |
| R4 — `payload.replyToId` vs top-level `replyTo` asymmetry gets collapsed (e.g., validator demands `payload.replyToId` matches top-level `replyTo`). | MEDIUM | Same shape as R3: add a dedicated unit test asserting the two fields are independent. JSDoc comment with rationale. |

## Acceptance Criteria

The impl is "done" when all of these hold (verifiable via `node tests/run.js` with `CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA=1` exiting zero plus targeted greps):

1. **`hooks/protocol/envelope.js` validates `summary` with explicit canonical-address rules.** Specifically: `validateEnvelope` rejects (in strict mode) an envelope with `payload.summary` set but no top-level `summary` for `kind ∈ {member-reply, proactive-report, thread-fanout, member-joined, member-left, stop-request, message, progress, question, done, blocked}`. Verified by a unit test in `tests/protocol-envelope-canonical.test.js`.
2. **`buildEnvelope` is called from every producer call-site** enumerated in the "Producer call-sites" table — verifiable by `rg "appendSystemMailbox\(" hooks/ | wc -l` matching `rg "buildEnvelope\(" hooks/` minus the in-validator self-reference. (Or: each of the 11 wrapped via the chokepoint mechanism.)
3. **`buildOutboxRow` is called from `stop.js:782` and `stop.js:839`** — verifiable by `rg "buildOutboxRow\(" hooks/stop.js` returning 2 hits.
4. **`CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA=1 node tests/run.js` exits zero** with all 218+ tests green. The +N new tests (S5, S6, S1 unit tests, expected ~10–15 new test files or assertions) also green.
5. **The v1.7.2 regression test exists and passes** — `tests/protocol-envelope-roundtrip.test.js` has an assertion block named (in comment) "v1.7.2 summary-drop regression" that constructs an envelope at `payload.summary` ONLY, runs `review-mail`, asserts the summary surfaces non-empty AND asserts a `schema-warning:` log line was emitted.
6. **Per-kind payload rules from the table above are enforced** — for each kind in the table, `tests/protocol-envelope-canonical.test.js` has one passing assertion that the required `payload.*` subfields validate clean and one passing assertion that the forbidden subfields trigger a strict-mode throw.
7. **Asymmetries explicitly preserved** — `tests/protocol-envelope-canonical.test.js` contains two named tests: "kind asymmetry preserved (env.kind ≠ env.from.kind validates)" and "replyTo asymmetry preserved (top-level replyTo on outbox AND payload.replyToId on system-mailbox member-reply BOTH validate)".
8. **Documentation updated** — `docs/protocol.md` has a "Canonical envelope field addresses" section with the per-field and per-kind tables; `README.md`'s `CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA` entry reflects required-in-CI; `CHANGELOG.md` has a v2.3.0 (or next minor) entry documenting the canonical-address contract and the deprecation timeline for the v1.7.3 dual-fix.
9. **`CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA` defaults to OFF in production.** A test runs `appendSystemMailbox` with a malformed payload and asserts that with the env var unset, the write succeeds (warn-only), and with `CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA=1` set, the write throws.
10. **No regressions to the 11 enumerated producer behaviours** — every existing producer test (`tests/proactive-report-notify.test.js`, `tests/send-receive-reply-cycle.test.js`, `tests/spawn-prompt-notify.test.js`, the `stop-*.test.js` family, `tests/threads-*.test.js`) passes unchanged. Where a test needs a per-test opt-out (e.g., it intentionally writes malformed input to test fallback behavior), the opt-out is documented in a comment in that test.
11. **Stretch only** — if S7 stretch GitHub Actions workflow is implemented: `.github/workflows/crews-tests.yml` exists, runs on PR touching `plugins/crews/**`, sets `CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA=1` in the env, and the latest push to the impl branch shows it passing.

## Preliminary Story Decomposition

Stories are sized for solo implementer + 30-minute review window each. Total estimated impl iterations: 5–7 (S1 + S2/S3 combined + S4 + S5 + S6 + S7).

- **S1 — `validateEnvelope` extension + `buildOutboxRow` factory + per-rule unit tests** (~2 iterations). Files: `hooks/protocol/envelope.js`, `tests/protocol-envelope-canonical.test.js` (NEW). No producer changes yet; validator can be loaded but is not yet wired into producers. Acceptance: criteria 1, 6, 7, 9.
- **S2 — Route `appendSystemMailbox` chokepoint through `buildEnvelope`** (~1 iteration). Files: `hooks/mailbox.js`. Acceptance: criterion 2 partial (7 of 11 producers covered).
- **S3 — Route remaining 4 producer call-sites individually** (~1 iteration). Files: `hooks/stop.js`, `hooks/commands/send-to-member.js`, `hooks/commands/send-to-thread.js`. Acceptance: criterion 2 full + criterion 3.
- **S4 — Enable `CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA=1` in `tests/run.js`** (~1 iteration). Files: `tests/run.js`, `README.md` (env-var doc only). Acceptance: criterion 4 (whole suite must go green; any pre-existing malformed-envelope tests are bugs revealed by S1–S3 plus this story).
- **S5 — Round-trip contract tests** (~1 iteration). Files: `tests/protocol-envelope-roundtrip.test.js` (NEW). Acceptance: criterion 4 (the new file must green) + criterion 10 (no regressions to existing producer tests).
- **S6 — v1.7.2 regression test** (~0.5 iteration; can be folded into S5 commit). Files: `tests/protocol-envelope-roundtrip.test.js` (extend). Acceptance: criterion 5.
- **S7 — Documentation + (stretch) GitHub Actions** (~1 iteration). Files: `docs/protocol.md`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, optionally `.github/workflows/crews-tests.yml`. Acceptance: criterion 8 (+ criterion 11 if stretch). Bump `package.json`-equivalent via `node plugins/crews/scripts/bump-version.js 2.3.0` per release runbook; run `node plugins/crews/tests/version.test.js` to verify all 6 manifest files agree.

**Stories order is load-bearing** — S2/S3 cannot ship before S1 (validator must exist to be called). S4 cannot pass green before S1–S3 (without producer wrapping, S4 turns on strict mode that catches malformed envelopes). S5/S6 are independent of S4 ordering (they test individual round-trips) but their assertions on strict-mode rejection only mean something after S1 ships. S7 can ship in parallel with S5/S6 but the CHANGELOG entry needs the final test count.

**Suggested decomposition for `/implement-with-ralph --parallel`:** Group A = {S1}, Group B = {S2, S3} (depends on A), Group C = {S4, S5, S6} (depends on B), Group D = {S7} (depends on C). Sequential implementation is also fine; the dependency chain is shallow.
